pending_round_policy.candidate_ranking: Score descending (high-value first), then obligation_id for stability
pending_round_policy.deduplication: By obligation_id (first occurrence wins), applied BEFORE truncation
pending_round_policy.mechanism_quota: Minimum 5 candidates per mechanism type (risk_family) guaranteed in pending
pending_round_policy.cost_estimation: Score-based ranking ensures low-value candidates are truncated first

answers.q1_what_is_pending_next_round: Queue of compiled obligations not selected in current round, carried to next planning round
answers.q2_why_600_truncated_legitimate: Large enterprise systems generate >600 valid obligations from state graph + analyzers + LLM reasoner; 600 was arbitrary legacy limit
answers.q3_truncated_mechanisms: Primarily deep mechanisms (cross-entity chain, idempotency replay) which generate many variants per entity
answers.q4_1200_project_e_specific: NO - 1200 is centralized _ABS_MAX_SLICE_BUDGET used by all projects via pipeline_slices.py
answers.q5_1200_candidate_explosion: Mitigated by: dedup, mechanism quota (5/type), score ranking, and auto-scaled per-round budget (drains pool in ~2 rounds)
answers.q6_ranking_priority: Yes - score descending, then obligation_id for deterministic stability
answers.q7_duplicate_candidates: Yes - dedup by obligation_id removes duplicates before truncation
answers.q8_memory_runtime_risk: Bounded: 1200 dicts * ~200 bytes = ~240KB max. No unbounded growth.
